# dsh-sage-mode · Sage Mode
English | 中文

A **read-only advisory mode** for DeepSeek Harness sessions.
Enter with `/sage`, leave with `/sage o

read-only advisory mode** for DeepSeek Harness sessions.
Enter with `/sage`, leave with `/sage off`.

While the mode is active, the session keeps only read/search/web tools. Every tool that
edits, delet

es, or executes is **hidden from the model** and **denied at execution**.
At the same time an adviso

ry system-prompt section turns the model into your thinking
partner: it answers, advises, evaluates,

explains, brainstorms, and diagnoses — instead of
changing your workspace.
The name comes from **Sage (贤者)**: the wise one gives counsel, not a hand.
## Why

Coding agents are built to act. Sometimes you do not want action — you want to understand
code, comp

are approaches, learn a concept, brainstorm, or debug an error. Sage mode gives
that intent a first-

class switch: the agent can still read your repository and search the
web, but it cannot touch anyth

s switch: the agent can still read your repository and search the
web, but it cannot touch anything.
## Usage
| Input | Effect |

| `/sage` | Enter Sage mode: read-only tools only, advisory prompt injected |
| `/sage <question>` |

Enter the mode **and** send that question as your next message (images/files allowed) |
| `/sage of
f` | Leave; the full toolset is restored immediately |

Typical uses: understanding an unfamiliar implementation, learning a codebase, comparing
design opti

ons, brainstorming, pasting a stack trace. When you are ready to actually change
code, run `/sage of

, brainstorming, pasting a stack trace. When you are ready to actually change
code, run `/sage off`.

Entering the mode changes what the model can call, not the sandbox: hidden tools are removed
from th

e request's tool catalog entirely, and anything that still reaches dispatch is refused
by a `tools.g
uard()` that returns "let the user run `/sage off` first".
## Tools kept (default)

`read` `read_image` `glob` `grep` `web_search` `web_fetch` `ask_user_question` `skill`
`cordis_inspe
ct_list` `cordis_inspect_query` `load_workspace_dependencies`

Everything else is hidden — `write` `edit` `ops_replace`, `pwsh`/`bash` and background jobs,
`subage

nt`/`send_message`, `plugin_manager`, `todo_write`, `present`, goal and team-task
tools, and so on.

Names that do not exist in your composition are ignored, so one list works
across agent presets.
## Reference
### Optional dependency: dsh-ops

The fast read-only tools — `ops_glob`, `ops_grep`, `ops_inspect_local_file` — come from
**dsh-ops**,

a separate bundle. Sage mode declares them
as an **optional dependency** (`optionalTools` in `cordi

ndle. Sage mode declares them
as an **optional dependency** (`optionalTools` in `cordis.patch.yml`):

- **dsh-ops installed** → those tools are adopted into the allow list and stay available.
- **dsh-op

s absent** → the names are ignored and everything else keeps working. A missing
optional provider is

names are ignored and everything else keeps working. A missing
optional provider is never an error.

The manager reads a GitHub repository URL as a git install spec, clones the package, adds its
`sage-

mode` row, and activates it. Updating later means installing the same URL again; a fresh
JavaScript
module generation needs an app restart to load.
Alternative: install from a local directory
From a checkout, point the manager at the absolute path instead:

That installs the package as a **link**, so editing files in the repo affects the live plugin
direct
ly — convenient while developing.
## Configuration

The row's defaults live in `cordis.patch.yml`. Your own overrides belong
in the profile's user layer

(`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`). A patch replaces
the targeted row's **whole** `conf
ig`, so restate every key you want to keep:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Unknown keys fail at load instead of being ignored, so a typo cannot silently disable your
configura
tion. Missing keys fall back to their defaults.
## How it works

- **State lives in the session log.** The mode folds the `command/run` + `command/done`
pair the com

mands service already writes, so it adds **no custom event type** — an
unknown event type would make

older readers refuse to reopen the session. Resume and fork
restore the mode automatically.
- **Enf

orced per agent.** `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({ allow })` hides the mutating tools and
`agent.ctx.too

ls.guard()` denies anything that still reaches dispatch. Both disposers are
owned by `agent.ctx` *an

d* kept in the plugin's own effect, so agent disposal and plugin
unload both unwind them.
- **Zero `

@deepseek-ai/*` dependencies.** A profile-installed bundle resolves those only from
the dsh installa

tion, so the plugin uses Node builtins plus services reached through `ctx`.
- The prompt section is

registered on the agent's own scope and returns an empty string while
the mode is off — no token cos

the agent's own scope and returns an empty string while
the mode is off — no token cost when unused.
## Known limits

- Applies to the **current session only**; other tabs and sessions are unaffected.
- Under PTC mode

the `run_code` transport itself is kept (otherwise the whole tool surface
becomes unusable), but the

generated SDK exposes only the permitted read-only tools.
- Plan mode's `exit_plan_mode` is hidden

too; leave plan mode with `/plan off` or `/sage off`.
- Sandbox and approval policy are unaffected —

this plugin governs **which tools the model
holds**, not filesystem permissions.
